answer: Coordinated-Origin Delay Pricing. Each new identity must anchor to a distinct arrival slot on a shared timeline; slots are allocated like berths off a jetty, one per origin per interval, so a batch of clones queues and pays escalating waiting costs. Because slot demand erodes slowly, like a glacier, attackers face months of delay before their fleet activates. A prism check splits each identity's arrival path into independently verified channels, so forged parallelism collapses into one slot. Cost: time plus per-slot fees, scaling with fleet size.
